title: What Happens When You Reel Up a Bass From 30 Feet?
hook: If you reel a bass up from 30 feet down, its body can't keep up.
script: If you reel a bass up from 30 feet down, its body can't keep up. A bass floats using a gas-filled swim bladder. Deep down, water pressure squeezes that gas small. Pull the fish up fast and the pressure drops, so the gas expands. The bladder swells, pushes on the stomach, and the fish can't swim back down. Anglers call it barotrauma. The fix is slow: bring deep fish up gently, and use a descender to send them home. Now you know why pros take their time.
